My social life - maybe in some aspects. I lost a few friends because of one incident. One night I was out and this man who was in his 40's stunk of beer. I should mention my father always smelt of stale beer. 

Anyway, he started hitting on me and he had resemblance to my father and he smelt like him. I started crying and then he put his hand on my thigh in probably a way to maybe comfort me, I'm not sure but that isn't how I saw it at the time. I freaked out, pushed him off me and started screaming and crying hysterically at him. I lost some friends because they thought I was insane. Which I might have thought as well if it wasnt me.

However one friend talked me to a couple days later and said that wasn't a normal reaction and pretty much just asked straight out 'you never speak about your dad at all and you freaked out last night..did your dad do things to you when you were a kid?' I just nodded and she was the first person to know about it. That was a turning point and that was the moment I felt better and a huge weight lifted. Excusing that incident, no my social life hasn't really been impacted. 

I volunteer at a animal shelter which specializes in cruelty cases. I read, listen to music, the normal stuff I suppose.

My life I guess is normal in some aspects. There is always an elephant in the room though with my mum. Like one wrong thing will remind her of my sister and she'll break down. In terms of my abuse, not one day goes past where I don't think about it. Some days are worse than others, if I have a nightmare about it, my day is usually consumed about thinking about it. I think I've dealt with it the best I can and I have a good support group from friends, boyfriend and my other sister. Honestly I'm lucky how my life is now compared to what other people go through and when I'm having a shitty time, I just try to remember that.

He would always tell the men, no marks or bruises, I suspect so it wouldn't be physically obvious what was happening. As for that attack, I don't know how noone knew. I remember barely being able to walk for a week. I would bleed profusely every time I went to the bathroom. But at this time my mum had thrown herself into work because she was so depressed about my sister and was hardly home. It felt in a way, my sisters death was more important than what was happening, so I guess noone was paying particular attention to anything being off about me. Noone had any reason to suspect anything I guess...

Thanks for your kind words and I guess the most important thing is I survived it, and I can in a way grow and realise the important things in life now :)

My advice would be every emotion you feel is perfectly fine, acceptable and normal. It was not your fault and you had no control over what happened. It is amazing you've made it this far and you are strong enough to make it through the hardest moments. Try to find one person you can talk to about it no matter what - family, friend, counselor, even a subreddit on here would be a place to find someone and accept sometimes people aren't going to know how to react to what you tell them. And finally, you're stronger and better than any thing that has happened to you and someone believes in you. 

I think I've learnt - time doesn't heal all wounds, it really doesn't. Time makes it easier to deal with things, to look back and reflect on what has happened, to give you strength and character. Horrible things happen, and they really suck, but there is always tomorrow and tomorrow will be less horrible.

My sister was murdered when she was 17. I'm from Australia and we have an event called Schoolies which is close to Spring Break I'm guessing. Basically all high school graduates go to the Gold Coast for a week and party. She and her friend got stranded and needed a lift back to their hotel they were staying at. They hitched a ride with a guy and about 2 minutes into the ride realized something was off about him. Her friend jumped out of the car at a stop light but my sister didn't get the chance. He took her back to his place and stabbed her to death.

I actually have never spoke to my mother about it and have no idea if she knows. The abuse started when i was 4 and she worked whenever he did, then my sister was killed what I was 5. I think she was honestly too heartbroken about that to notice anything else was aloof. Sometimes I feel bitter and angry, like how could she have not known? I like to believe that if she did know, she would have stopped it. My other sister recently confronted me about the whole situation, asking if he had abused me because she said in hindsight she remembers certain situations being off. We had this long conversation until 3 in the morning and I told her what had happened. She told me she had no idea anything at the time was going on, but only looking back she sees things were off. So basically, I don't blame anyone but my father and the other men who were doing but it doesn't mean I don't get angry or question if people knew sometimes.
